about: How savings interest is taxed, for tools/build-savings-tax-pages.js. UK rules quoted from GOV.UK; other countries from the official source in each entry. Rates are for 2026 unless stated.

allowances.quote: Your allowances for earning interest before you have to pay tax on it include your: Personal Allowance; starting rate for savings; Personal Savings Allowance. You get these allowances each tax year (6 April to 5 April).

startingRate.quote: If your other taxable income (not including savings interest or dividends) is less than £17,570, you can get the starter rate for savings. This means you can earn up to £5,000 of interest and not have to pay tax on it. … Every £1 of other income above your Personal Allowance reduces your starting rate for savings by £1. Example: You earn £16,000 of wages and £200 interest on your savings … Your remaining starting rate for savings is £1,570 … you will not have to pay tax on your £200 savings interest.

psa.quote: To work out your tax band, add all the interest you’ve earned to your other income. Basic rate £1,000; Higher rate £500; Additional rate £0 … Your Personal Savings Allowance is £1,000 because you’re a basic rate taxpayer. This means that the: first £1,000 is not taxed; remaining £300 is taxed at 20% (basic rate); tax due on your savings interest is £60

rate.quote: You pay tax on any interest over your allowance at your usual rate of Income Tax.

isa.quote: You do not usually have to pay tax on interest earned from savings in accounts like Individual Savings Accounts (ISAs) and some National Savings and Investments.

scotland.quote: You’ll pay the same tax as the rest of the UK on dividends and savings interest.

rates2027.quote: Savings income tax rates from 6 April 2027: 24% basic, 44% higher, 49% additional (Budget 2026 OOTLAR Annex A, as in the site's April 2027 guide).

collection.quote: If you have tax to pay on your savings interest, HMRC will send you a tax calculation. These are usually sent between June and the end of November. HMRC will usually collect the tax through your tax code.

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: Taxable interest is reported on your federal return and taxed with your other income at your normal rates (10% to 37%); states have their own rules.
countries.quote: You must report all taxable and tax-exempt interest on your federal income tax return, even if you don't receive a Form 1099-INT or Form 1099-OID.

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Interest is included in your income and taxed at your normal federal and provincial rates.

source.title: Income Tax Act, section 12 (income inclusions: interest)

countries.quote: …any amount received or receivable by the taxpayer in the year … as, on account of, in lieu of payment of or in satisfaction of, interest to the extent that the interest was not included in computing the taxpayer’s income for a preceding taxation year

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: Banks deduct Deposit Interest Retention Tax (DIRT) at 33% before paying the interest.

source.title: Revenue Ready Reckoner, post Budget 2027 (DIRT section)

countries.quote: Deposit Interest Retention Tax (DIRT): Reduction in the standard rate of DIRT, From 33% to 31% … Increase in the standard rate of DIRT, From 33% to 35%

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: Interest above the €1,000 saver's allowance (€2,000 for a married couple) is taxed at the 25% flat withholding tax plus 5.5% solidarity surcharge on it (26.375%), and church tax if you pay it. If your own rate is lower, you can choose it in your tax return.
countries.quote: durch den Steuerabzug (Abgeltungsteuer) von 25 Prozent zuzüglich Solidaritätszuschlag und ggf. Kirchensteuer abgegolten … unter dem Sparer-Pauschbetrag von 1.000 Euro (bzw. 2.000 Euro …)

countries.name: France
countries.summary: Most interest is taxed at the 31.4% flat tax (prélèvement forfaitaire unique), which covers income tax and social charges; you can choose the income tax scale instead.

source.title: Service Public — CSG déductible (flat tax rate)

countries.quote: Prélèvement forfaitaire unique (PFU), appelé également flat tax au taux de 31,4 % (ou de 30 %)

countries.name: Spain
countries.summary: Interest is part of the savings income base, taxed on its own scale: 19% up to €6,000, 21% to €50,000, 23% to €200,000, 27% to €300,000 and 30% above.

source.title: Ley 35/2006 del IRPF, arts. 66 and 76 (BOE consolidated text)

countries.quote: Base liquidable del ahorro: 0–6.000 9,5; 6.000–50.000 10,5; 50.000–200.000 11,5; 200.000–300.000 13,5; en adelante 15 (state scale, art. 66; the regional scale in art. 76 is the same)

countries.name: Japan
countries.summary: Interest on deposits is taxed at 20.315% (15.315% national income tax including the reconstruction surtax, plus 5% local tax), withheld at source, and that settles it.

source.title: National Tax Agency, Tax Answer No. 1310 (interest income)

countries.quote: 利子所得の金額に一律15.315パーセント（他に地方税5パーセント）の税率を乗じて算出した所得税および復興特別所得税…が源泉徴収され、これにより納税が完結する
